projects.name: OverSync
projects.description:
OverSync is listed in the Drips catalog of repositories approved for the Stellar
Wave Program. A Hub search for `OverSync` returned zero public matches when this
research was prepared, so it was not already listed in the Hub.

## What OverSync Does

OverSync is a non-custodial bridge for moving native assets between Ethereum and
Stellar. Its central problem is the trust placed in many cross-chain bridges:
an off-chain validator set or attester can approve a destination release even
when the source-side lock is not real. OverSync uses symmetric hash-time-lock
contracts instead. Both sides lock funds against the same cryptographic hash,
and the swap settles when the beneficiary reveals the secret. If the secret is
not revealed before the deadline, the relevant contract exposes a permissionless
refund path.

The live v2 design has a Solidity HTLC on Ethereum Sepolia and a Soroban HTLC on
Stellar Testnet. The Stellar side also has a resolver registry that manages
resolver participation and staking. A resolver can provide liquidity and
complete the other side of a swap, but it does not receive a privileged route
to move user funds. The coordinator is an off-chain matching and metadata
service; the repository states that it does not hold keys capable of signing
HTLC transactions. The frontend is explicitly testnet-only while the v2
contracts go through the project's audit and governance gates.

The swap sequence is designed around different timelocks. The user locks ETH
under a SHA-256 hash, the resolver locks XLM under the same hash with a shorter
deadline, the user claims XLM by revealing the preimage, and the resolver uses
that public preimage to claim ETH. The asymmetry gives the user a recovery
window if the swap does not complete. The Soroban implementation contains the
HTLC lifecycle, refund logic, resolver-registry integration, and contract tests;
the repository also includes a TypeScript coordinator, resolver runner,
frontend, and event polling service.

OverSync should be represented as Testnet infrastructure, not as a production
mainnet bridge. Its own documentation says the v2 deployment is unaudited and
that mainnet is gated on additional testing, governance, and an independent
audit. That limitation is part of an accurate project profile because the
protocol handles locked assets even though this particular deployment is for
testnet evaluation.
projects.tags: cross-chain, bridge, soroban, htlc, non-custodial, ethereum, stellar-wave

projects.name: AgentPay
projects.description:
AgentPay is a testnet payment system for autonomous software agents. Its core
problem is that an agent needs enough authority to pay for a service, but should
not receive unrestricted access to a person's wallet or secret key. AgentPay
models that authority as a capped, expiring, and revocable on-chain delegation.
A human grants the initial permission through a wallet signature, then the agent
can make purchases within the stated limit. The design gives the owner a way to
end the authority rather than relying on an off-chain promise that an agent will
behave.

The repository separates this into three Soroban contracts. The Agent Registry
stores the agent identity and reputation data. The Delegation Manager records
the spending allowance and enforces its limits. The Marketplace records
services and drives a purchase flow that checks the delegation before a payment
is completed. This is more than a frontend that labels a normal wallet transfer
as agentic: the limit check and related state transitions are intended to run
in Soroban, while the application uses Freighter for the human authorization
step and Stellar USDC for the demo settlement asset.

The project also exposes a web demonstration, frontend tests, Rust contract
tests, deployment scripts, and an activity feed that links transactions to
Stellar Expert. Its material correctly describes the deployment as testnet,
which matters for evaluating it: AgentPay demonstrates a concrete approach to
controlled autonomous payments, but it should not be represented as a mainnet
financial product. The project is well suited to the Payments category because
its central function is permission-scoped USDC payment execution rather than
general AI tooling.

projects.name: Sanctifier
projects.description:
Sanctifier is a security copilot and formal verification suite built specifically for Stellar Soroban smart contracts. When Soroban shipped to mainnet in 2024, the ecosystem inherited almost none of the auditing tooling that has been standard on EVM chains for years — no static analysis framework tuned to Soroban's authorization model, no runtime guard primitives, no CVE-style vulnerability database, and no CI-ready badge pipeline. Every team was re-discovering the same five footguns from scratch on every audit. Sanctifier is the missing layer.

The project ships one engine — sanctifier-core — across five surfaces: a Rust CLI (sanctifier-cli, installable via cargo, npm/npx, Homebrew, Scoop, and winget), a GitHub Action that uploads SARIF to GitHub code-scanning, a Next.js web dashboard for drag-and-drop scanning and report exploration, a VS Code extension that provides inline diagnostics as you type, and a set of on-chain Soroban runtime guard contracts deployed to testnet that emit verifiable audit events after every guarded invocation.

At its heart are twelve canonical detection rules, coded S001–S012. S001 catches missing require_auth on state-changing functions — the most common drain vector on Soroban. S002 flags panic!/unwrap/expect in contract paths that permanently lock state. S003 detects unchecked arithmetic that causes silent loss-of-funds rounding. S004 warns on ledger entries approaching the size threshold that causes mid-transaction write failures. S005 finds storage-key collisions between data paths. S006 flags unsafe patterns including timestamp-as-randomness. S007 enforces custom YAML rules so teams can codify house style. S008 catches inconsistent or missing event emissions that blind wallets and indexers. S009 flags unhandled Result return values that mask silent failures. S010 surfaces upgrade/admin/governance risk like single-key takeover paths. S011 is backed by a Z3 SMT solver and disproves mathematical invariants. S012 detects SEP-41 token interface deviations that cause wallets to reject the token.

Beyond static analysis, Sanctifier maintains a community vulnerability database (data/vulnerability-db.json) that maps known CVE-style patterns (SOL-2024-*) to AST signatures — a published exploit anywhere instantly becomes a detection everywhere. A growing Z001–Z014 series covers zero-knowledge contract pitfalls: nullifiers that are never recorded, public inputs that do not commit to the transaction, and verifying keys pulled straight from storage without ceremony provenance.

The runtime guard contracts on testnet — CBLDEREKXK6AIZ7ZSKC6VYCK4MKF4FZ4ANJEU67QZAQUG57I4KGZMTXB (Runtime Guard Wrapper), CDDVM5A5IVDAG5FZ2OU2CLWAHC7A2T7LHQHZSDVKZPE6SDMDO2JCR3UY (Reentrancy Guard), and CABBT5FKG7AE7IEEA4KR2J5AVYRSZAWKTXZ2KFX3UNJQAMMLMCXNLMIB (Vulnerable-by-design demo) — are live and respond to health_check, get_stats, and get_call from any caller. They emit on-chain events observable via Stellar Expert, producing a forensic audit trail that survives the lifetime of the wrapped contract.

With 116 community forks, ~100 hand-curated contrib-wave issues, a JSON Schema-validated output format, SARIF 2.1.0 output for GitHub code-scanning, and a Dockerfile for zero-install CI, Sanctifier is built to be the standard security gate for Soroban development the way Slither and Foundry are for the EVM ecosystem.

projects.name: SafeTrust
projects.description:
SafeTrust is a decentralized peer-to-peer escrow platform that secures booking deposits for hotels, vacation rentals, and tourism operators on the Stellar network — removing intermediaries from a market historically dominated by centralized booking platforms. When a guest books a property, the deposit is locked into a Soroban smart-contract escrow created through the TrustlessWork Escrow-as-a-Service API, and funds are released in milestones as both parties confirm fulfillment, or returned on dispute. The core flow is fully on-chain: the tenant pays, signs an unsigned XDR in a Stellar wallet (Freighter, Albedo, or LOBSTR), funds lock on testnet, and every release is a Stellar transaction.

Under the hood, SafeTrust is a multi-tenant platform: a Node/Express webhook service owns the escrow lifecycle (initialize → fund → approve-milestone → release-funds, plus dispute → resolve-dispute), with HMAC-verified TrustlessWork webhooks; Hasura GraphQL + PostgreSQL store escrow state per tenant (safetrust and hotel_industry schemas); the Next.js 15 frontend uses Apollo Client with Firebase auth plus wallet sync; and an Astro landing page markets the product. Unusually for a Wave project, the backend ships Rust crates as native Node addons (Neon): stellar-utils for Stellar address validation and Ed25519 signature verification, plus a soroban-reconciler used by a reconciliation cron that periodically syncs on-chain contract state back into the database and detects drift between off-chain and on-chain ledgers. A Karate test suite exercises the full escrow lifecycle state machine (deploying → funded → completed / disputed → resolved).

On-chain evidence: SafeTrust's platform account GBPA2LO4XHBZD54ZEGGK4GG3OYHAYBPK6FNDAHCJWNJTLTKYUL52QCQR is live on Stellar testnet (sequence 17648952627167233), holding a USDC trustline (2.2 USDC) and 9999.99 XLM, with recent invoke_host_function (Soroban) transactions on ledgers 4109217–4110182 (Aug 12, 2026). Escrows settle in USDC through the testnet USDC Stellar Asset Contract (CBIELTK6YBZJU5UP2WWQEUCYKLPU6AUNZ2BQ4WWFEIE3USCIHMXQDAMA). The team is also building SafeTrust ZK — a Noir zero-knowledge pipeline (proof-of-funds, private escrow amount, and milestone-release proofs) that adds privacy to the escrow lifecycle on Stellar's BN254 curve, positioning the platform for compliant, confidential hospitality payments.

projects.name: MERCATO
projects.description:
MERCATO is a supply chain finance application built on the Stellar network that helps small and medium businesses (PyMEs — pequeñas y medianas empresas) in Latin America buy inventory with investor-funded escrow, pay suppliers in milestones as work is proven, and settle in USDC. The platform addresses a critical gap: traditional banks rarely provide short-term working capital to PyMEs in emerging markets, leaving them unable to purchase inventory or pay suppliers on time.

At its core, MERCATO composes multiple Stellar ecosystem products into a unified platform. Trustless Work provides non-custodial multi-release escrow contracts — deal funding stays in smart contract rules, not the platform's bank account. When a PyME creates a deal, escrow is deployed via Trustless Work, signed with their Stellar wallet (Freighter or Albedo through Stellar Wallets Kit), and investors fund it directly in USDC. As suppliers deliver and milestones are approved, the escrow contract releases payment in stages — every release is an on-chain Stellar transaction.

MERCATO integrates Blend Soroban lending pools as a Stellar-native liquidity layer alongside deal escrow, and DeFindex Soroban yield vaults for multi-strategy allocation of idle capital. For fiat access, it supports multiple ramp providers including Etherfuse (Mexico SPEI), Alfred Pay (LATAM), BlindPay (global), and MoneyGram Stellar ramps — all implemented through SEP protocol modules (SEP-1, 6, 10, 12, 24, 31, 38). The app is built with Next.js 16, React 19, Tailwind CSS, and Supabase for auth and off-chain state.

MERCATO is a verified Stellar Wave Program participant with 4x Points weighting, 2 GitHub stars, 17 forks, and 149 commits across its repository. The project has comprehensive documentation including architecture diagrams, setup guides, and contribution guidelines. Its modular design — combining escrow, wallets, lending, yield vaults, and fiat ramps from across the Stellar ecosystem — makes it a strong example of Stellar's composability for real-world financial infrastructure.

projects.name: PromptHash
projects.description:
PromptHash is a decentralized marketplace on the Stellar network that enables creators to sell AI prompts as licensed digital assets. Instead of transferring ownership, it focuses on controlled access, where buyers purchase usage rights while the actual prompt content remains encrypted and protected.

Built using Soroban smart contracts, the platform handles prompt listings, pricing, purchase tracking, and fee distribution directly on-chain. Creators publish encrypted prompt assets with public preview metadata, while buyers pay in XLM to gain access rights recorded by the contract.

After purchase, access is verified through a wallet-based authentication system. Buyers sign a challenge message to prove ownership of the purchasing wallet, and the backend verifies this alongside on-chain access data before decrypting and delivering the prompt.

This design ensures transparent payments, secure content distribution, and verifiable licensing without relying on centralized platforms. It extends Stellar’s utility beyond simple transfers by enabling programmable commerce for digital goods. PromptHash Stellar can be applied to other assets like templates, datasets, and educational content, making it a foundation for encrypted creator marketplaces on-chain.
projects.tags: AI Prompt Marketplace, Creator Economy,  XLM Digital Licensing, Web3 Commerce

projects.name: Akkuea
projects.description:
Akkuea is an institutional-grade decentralized finance (DeFi) architecture designed to bridge the structural divide between traditional real estate asset management and on-chain liquidity frameworks. By leveraging the high-throughput and low-fee capabilities of the Stellar network, Akkuea provides a dual-faceted ecosystem: it resolves structural asset illiquidity via fractionalized property tokenization and scales DeFi utility by allowing tangible real-world assets (RWAs) to safely serve as debt collateral.

On a technical level, the platform utilizes a unified Bun monorepo environment separating its workspaces into a Next.js 16/React 19 web interface, a high-performance Elysia backend REST API, and a custom suite of Rust smart contracts running on the modern Soroban SDK v25. The core tokenization contract mechanisms handle fractional share management while enforcing strict KYC/AML compliance checks natively on-chain via role-based access configurations. For its credit mechanics, Akkuea incorporates automated interest calculation parameters, oracle-driven valuation tools for collateral ratios, and privacy-configurable parameters designed explicitly for institutional lending markets.

Furthermore, Akkuea secures user data profiles by omitting centralized credential databases entirely, relying instead on wallet-based cryptographic authentication powered by Stellar signatures via @creit.tech/stellar-wallets-kit. This programmatic architecture ensures complete auditability, transforming off-chain property histories into immutable, indexable on-chain tracking logs. Ultimately, the system stands out as a highly secure, scalable roadmap demonstrating how modern Web3 runtimes like Bun and Soroban can be combined to implement highly complex, compliant real-world asset primitives on the Stellar ledger.

projects.name: Lance
projects.description:
Lance is a decentralized freelance marketplace built on the Stellar network that combines Soroban smart contracts, Stellar USDC payments, and AI-powered dispute resolution. The platform is designed to make freelancing more transparent and secure by eliminating common issues such as payment delays, non-payment, and biased dispute handling.

When a client posts a job, funds are locked in a Soroban escrow contract, ensuring that payment is available before work begins. As project milestones are completed and approved, payments are released automatically using Stellar USDC, enabling fast and low-cost transactions across borders.

A standout feature of Lance is its AI Agent Judge, which helps resolve disputes between clients and freelancers. The AI reviews project requirements, submitted work, and supporting evidence to provide an impartial decision, reducing the need for traditional human arbitration.

The platform also includes an on-chain reputation system that records user activity and work history through Soroban smart contracts. This creates a transparent reputation layer that helps users build trust over time.

By combining blockchain-based escrow, decentralized reputation, and AI-driven dispute resolution, Lance offers a modern approach to freelancing that leverages Stellar's speed, affordability, and smart contract capabilities.
projects.tags: freelance, remote work

projects.name: StellarMicroPay
projects.description:
Stellar MicroPay lets anyone send tiny payments across borders instantly — for fractions of a cent. No bank. No borders. No friction.
Send XLM to anyone with a Stellar address, anywhere in the world. Transactions confirm in 3–5 seconds and cost ~0.00001 XLM, so sending $0.01 or $1,000 costs the same. It's fully non-custodial — your keys, your funds. We never touch your private key.
Features instant settlement, global reach across 100+ countries, micro fees, and a beginner-friendly explainer for newcomers to Stellar.
Open source · MIT License · Built with Next.js on the Stellar network.

projects.name: StellarKit
projects.description:
StellarKit (formerly known as Stellar Suite) is a high-performance, browser-based Integrated Development Environment (IDE) engineered to streamline the end-to-end development, testing, and deployment cycles of Soroban Rust smart contracts on the Stellar blockchain network. 

Bypassing the friction of traditional local toolchain setups, rustup installations, or local system dependency conflicts, StellarKit brings an absolute desktop-grade software development workflow natively to the web browser. The platform functions as a full-scale developer launchpad, featuring an advanced layout equipped with a multi-file system navigation drawer, a custom Monaco-driven source code workspace, and real-time execution sandboxes.

The web-based engine empowers developers to create, customize, and prototype smart contracts using clean pre-loaded boilerplate templates. Through a beautifully intuitive client panel, engineers can smoothly switch between open file buffers, trace syntax updates, and prepare their logic profiles for immediate testing. By introducing an in-browser suite that eliminates setup barriers, StellarKit significantly accelerates the developer onboarding curve, allowing Web3 programmers to move from initial concept lines to functional Soroban logic entirely within a unified, web-accessible development workspace.

projects.name: Stellar Portfolio Rebalancer
projects.description:
Stellar Portfolio Rebalancer is an automated DeFi portfolio manager built to maintain optimal asset allocations on the Stellar network. Users define their target weights (e.g., 40% XLM, 35% USDC, 25% BTC) and a drift tolerance threshold. When market movements cause the portfolio to drift, the platform automatically triggers rebalancing trades directly on the Stellar DEX.

The core logic is powered by a Soroban smart contract written in Rust, which securely handles portfolio state and tracks allocations. Asset pricing is driven by Reflector oracles (with CoinGecko as a fallback) to ensure accurate, tamper-proof valuation. Trades are executed via the @stellar/stellar-sdk using slippage-aware mechanisms that manage partial fills and rollbacks gracefully.

Designed with enterprise-grade safety, the platform features a 1-hour rebalance cooldown, volatility circuit breakers, and concentration limits to prevent over-allocation. Due to Soroban ledger entry size constraints, portfolios support a maximum of 10 assets. Backed by a highly active community with over 510 commits, 79 forks, and 188 issues, this robust stack—combining a React/TypeScript frontend, Node.js/Express backend, and PostgreSQL—delivers a seamless, hands-off asset management experience on Stellar Testnet.
projects.tags: defi, portfolio, rebalancing, soroban, reflector, oracle, stellar-dex, stellar-wave

projects.name: CarbonChain
projects.description:
CarbonChain is a transparent, tamper-proof carbon credit registry and marketplace built natively on the Stellar network. Designed as a Soroban-native platform, it enables the tokenized issuance, trading, and retirement of carbon credits while enforcing real-world climate accountability. The project supports multiple environmental methodologies, including REDD+, VCS (Verra), Gold Standard, and Plan Vivo, providing a highly configurable setup for emerging climate standards.

From a technical perspective, CarbonChain operates on a robust five-layer architecture: Rust/WASM Soroban smart contracts, the Stellar public ledger, a NestJS REST API, an Angular 17+ frontend, and off-chain storage utilizing PostgreSQL and IPFS. The smart contract layer is divided into four distinct components: CreditRegistry for minting and multi-sig enforcement, Retirement for immutable token burning, Marketplace for active listings, and an MRV Oracle for anomaly detection via IoT and satellite data ingestion. Recently, the platform expanded to include a marketplace fee collection mechanism within the contracts and a Soroban events indexer in the NestJS API to poll the RPC for lifecycle events every 30 seconds.

CarbonChain's Stellar integration is highly optimized. Instead of building a custom Automated Market Maker (AMM), it utilizes Stellar's built-in Decentralized Exchange (DEX) to list Carbon Credit (CCR) tokens directly against XLM and USDC via manage_sell_offer operations. The project also leverages Stellar Claimable Balances to securely escrow credits during the verifier approval window, and utilizes SEP-10 challenge-response flows through the Freighter wallet for secure, keyless user authentication.
projects.tags: Soroban, Smart Contracts, Carbon Credits, MRV, Stellar DEX, NestJS, Angular

projects.name: RouteDock
projects.description:
Before RouteDock, building an AI agent that paid for services on Stellar meant picking a protocol—x402, MPP Charge, or MPP Session—and wiring up integration code for each one. Three protocols, three SDKs, three separate mental models. Every team was writing the same plumbing from scratch.
RouteDock wraps all three into one function call: client.pay(). The agent reads a provider's routedock.json manifest, the right mode gets selected automatically, and that's the end of the agent's involvement. No conditional logic. No rework when a provider changes protocols.
Each mode handles a different cost tradeoff. x402 runs per-request HTTP 402 flows via USDC SAC transfer. MPP Charge is per-action with no facilitator and lower fees. MPP Session offloads interactions entirely — ed25519 vouchers settle off-chain, so 50 interactions produce two on-chain transactions total. Spend limits are enforced inside __check_auth at the Soroban contract level, so an overspend gets rejected before anything broadcasts.
The SDK ships as @routedock/routedock on npm. Contracts are Rust/Soroban. There's a Next.js dashboard at routedock.xyz and two live provider APIs running on testnet.

projects.name: Lumenpulse
projects.description:
Lumenpulse is a high-performance, decentralized cryptocurrency news aggregation, sentiment analysis, and multi-asset portfolio management ecosystem built natively within the Stellar blockchain network. Designed to resolve the core vulnerabilities of centralized information silos, market manipulation, and unreliable media streams, Lumenpulse provides an open-source framework that rewards verified community content curation. The platform empowers users with real-time, borderless market insights while utilizing specialized, programmatic on-chain reward loops to incentivize accurate technical reporting and decentralized journalism.

The platform relies on an intuitive, futuristic client interface structured across two primary consumer dashboards: an automated News Aggregation Dashboard that ingests multi-source data and a Portfolio Visualization suite. projects.name: Stellopay
projects.description: Stellopay is an open-source, decentralized payroll infrastructure built entirely on Stellar's Soroban smart contract platform. It allows employers to deposit salary tokens into a contract-managed balance pool and configure recurring payment schedules for employees, with amounts and recurrence frequency defined per worker. The system automatically tracks payment eligibility and releases funds when the scheduled time is reached. Employees can trigger their own withdrawals without waiting for employer action, providing self-sovereign access to earned wages. Employers can also process bulk disbursements for many employees in a single transaction, making it practical for organisations with large workforces. Unlike most payroll tools that rely on centralised intermediaries or third-party escrow services, Stellopay implements its own full Soroban contract from scratch with typed storage, comprehensive error handling across 10 error types, a full event emission system, and an admin emergency pause mechanism. The contract supports any Stellar asset as a salary token — not just USDC — making it flexible for any organisation operating on Stellar. The frontend is a Next.js 14 TypeScript application with a merchant dashboard, account summary, notification panel, and settings interface, already deployed live on Vercel. The project has two active repositories in the Stellar Wave Program with a combined 167 forks and 685 commits, and carries a 4x Points multiplier on Drips.

projects.name: Wraith
projects.description:
Wraith is a Stellar infrastructure project that indexes incoming Soroban token transfers by recipient address, a query pattern that Horizon does not provide for Stellar Asset Contract and SEP-41 token events. Its core value is practical: wallets, payment apps, bots, dashboards, and accounting tools often need to answer what did this address receive without running their own event decoder. Wraith fills that gap by polling Stellar RPC getEvents, decoding CAP-67 and SEP-41 token events, storing normalized transfer records in Postgres, and exposing both REST endpoints and WebSocket subscriptions for address-level transfer monitoring.

The technical design is deliberately small and indexer-focused. The startIndexer loop tracks the latest ledger, fetches Soroban contract events in batches, and routes them through fetchEventsSafe. That safe fetcher is important because the README documents a bisection strategy for protocol/XDR decoding errors: if one ledger in a range cannot be decoded, the range is split until the problematic ledger is isolated, logged, skipped, and indexing continues. Parsed events are converted into typed records covering transfer, mint, burn, and clawback, then persisted with duplicate protection. Query APIs such as /transfers/incoming/:address, /transfers/outgoing/:address, /transfers/address/:address, /transfers/tx/:txHash, and /summary/:address make the indexed data directly useful to downstream applications.

Wraith uses Stellar through Soroban RPC rather than a custom contract. The project watches configured Stellar Asset Contract IDs via SAC_CONTRACT_IDS or CONTRACT_IDS; when unset, it defaults to the native XLM SAC for the selected network. The testnet native XLM SAC published in source is CDMLFMKMMD7MWZP3FKUBZPVHTUEDLSX4BYGYKH4GCESXYHS3IHQ4EIG4, and Stellar Expert's testnet contract API resolves it successfully. The README also documents mainnet configuration expectations and explains that production mainnet deployments should use an explicit Soroban RPC provider plus a constrained contract filter, for example native XLM and USDC SACs, to avoid scanning unnecessary event volume.

This makes Wraith a strong Stellar Wave Hub entry even though it is not a consumer dApp: it is ecosystem plumbing. It improves observability for Soroban token movement, makes address-centric incoming payment detection easier, and turns raw Stellar RPC events into application-friendly data.

projects.name: ACTA
projects.description: ACTA is a verifiable credentials infrastructure for the Stellar blockchain that enables businesses and platforms to issue, store, verify, and revoke W3C Verifiable Credentials 2.0 entirely on-chain using Soroban smart contracts. The platform addresses a fundamental gap in blockchain-based compliance: the need for tamper-proof, privacy-preserving credential management that satisfies regulatory requirements without centralizing sensitive user data. At its core, ACTA provides a zero databases architecture where encrypted credential payloads are anchored directly on the Stellar ledger and managed through a unified smart contract called vc-vault. There is no backend database storing credentials. Instead, each user controls a personal vault on-chain, and only they can decrypt the contents. Issuers such as banks, fintech platforms, and compliance providers can issue credentials into a user vault after being explicitly authorized by the vault owner, enforcing user consent at the protocol level. The credential lifecycle is deterministic and publicly auditable. Every credential passes through well-defined states Active, Revoked, or Expired with each transition recorded as a Soroban contract event. Verifiers including regulators, partner platforms, and auditors can check a credential status by querying the contract directly, receiving a cryptographic proof of the current state without needing to contact the issuer or access the holder private data. For regulatory compliance, ACTA enables platforms to issue KYC/AML credentials that prove a user has passed identity verification without re-exposing their personal documents. A fintech app can issue a KYC Passed credential after onboarding a user, and any downstream service in the Stellar ecosystem can verify that credential on-chain in one call, eliminating redundant KYC checks while maintaining compliance with Anti-Money Laundering regulations. The platform also supports zero-knowledge proofs via Noir circuits for selective disclosure, allowing users to prove specific attributes such as age over 18 or residency in a particular jurisdiction without revealing any other personal information, directly supporting GDPR data minimization principles.

projects.name: CurrentDao

projects.name: Anchor-Kit
projects.description:
Anchor-Kit is a developer-friendly, type-safe TypeScript SDK for building Stellar Anchor services. It abstracts the complexity of Stellar Ecosystem Proposals — specifically SEP-6, SEP-24 (Hosted Deposit and Withdrawal), and SEP-31 (Cross-Border Payments) — allowing developers to focus on business logic while ensuring protocol compliance and security.

The SDK provides a complete anchor implementation out of the box. SEP-24 Interactive Flows give hosted deposit and withdrawal flows with minimal configuration — developers mount a single Express router and get fully compliant interactive deposit and withdrawal endpoints instantly. SEP-10 Authentication provides built-in Stellar Web Authentication handling, managing challenge generation, signature verification, and JWT token issuance without requiring developers to understand the underlying cryptography.

Anchor-Kit also includes background job processing for transaction monitoring, automatic settlement triggering, and configurable retry logic for failed settlements. It supports SQLite for development and PostgreSQL for production via a database adapter pattern. Built-in webhook signature verification enables real-time notifications to partner systems.

The SDK integrates directly with Stellar Horizon API for account queries, transaction submission, and status monitoring. It supports testnet, mainnet, and futurenet with automatic network passphrase resolution. The library ships with 85+ unit tests covering configuration validation, error handling, database adapters, queue processing, and webhook verification — indicating production-ready engineering standards suitable for fintech and payment providers connecting to the Stellar network.

projects.name: PetAd
projects.description:
PetAd is a full-stack pet adoption and temporary custody management platform powered by Stellar blockchain trust guarantees. The platform enables users to browse pets, initiate adoption processes, and manage temporary custody arrangements — with all financial settlements handled transparently on-chain via Stellar escrow accounts.

The system addresses three critical problems in traditional pet adoption:

1. Trust Gap — Adopters and shelters have no trustless mechanism to ensure funds are only released when adoption conditions are met. PetAd solves this with Stellar escrow accounts that lock funds until both parties confirm completion.

2. Dispute Resolution — When adoptions go wrong (misrepresented health conditions, custody violations), there is typically no neutral arbitration mechanism. PetAd implements a full dispute system with escrow settlement pausing, evidence submission, and admin-mediated resolution.

3. Transparency — All financial flows are recorded on the Stellar blockchain, giving shelters, adopters, and regulators full visibility into transaction history via Stellar Horizon API.

PetAd uses Stellar specifically for multi-signature escrow accounts, XLM payment operations, transaction memo encoding for on-chain auditability, real-time Horizon API polling, and cryptographic trust hashing anchored to Stellar transaction hashes. The SDK includes buildPaymentOp(), decodeMemo(), createEscrowAccount(), lockCustodyFunds(), and anchorTrustHash() — all built on @stellar/stellar-sdk.

projects.name: Soroban-ZK-Std
projects.description:
Soroban-ZK-Std is a high-performance, modular, no_std cryptographic standard library optimized for the Soroban Virtual Machine on Stellar. It provides the mathematical primitives required to build and verify Zero Knowledge proofs on-chain, including Groth16 proof verification — the most widely used ZK proof system in production blockchain applications today.

The library directly leverages Protocol 25 (CAP-0075) host functions: bn254_multi_pairing_check for native BN254 pairing verification and poseidon2_permutation for hashing — 47% faster than software alternatives. It is structured into zk-core (pure BN254 field and curve arithmetic), zk-soroban (Soroban host function bindings), and verifier-sample (WASM size and gas validation). All operations are constant-time to prevent side-channel attacks.

The scalar multiplication implementation runs at ~17M instructions, well within Soroban's 400M budget. The library enables shielded RWA transfers, ZK-voting for DAOs, configurable privacy for institutional payments, and Groth16 proof verification on Stellar — use cases previously impossible without this foundational tooling.
projects.tags: zk, groth16, bn254, soroban, cryptography, no_std, stellar-wave, privacy, infrastructure

projects.name: KindFi
projects.description:
KindFi is an open-source Web3 crowdfunding platform built on Stellar, purpose-built to connect donors with verified social and environmental causes — primarily across Latin America. Unlike traditional donation platforms, KindFi enforces accountability at the protocol level: every campaign runs through milestone-based Soroban smart contract escrows, meaning funds are only released when a project demonstrates verifiable progress. This eliminates the trust gap that plagues conventional charity platforms.

The platform is a full-stack monorepo (TypeScript + Rust) with five distinct on-chain contract systems deployed on Stellar Soroban: (1) an Auth system using WebAuthn-compatible Secp256r1 signatures with an Account Factory, Auth Controller, and individual Account contracts for decentralized identity; (2) an NFT contract ("Kinders") using the OpenZeppelin NonFungibleToken standard for contributor recognition; (3) Soulbound Academy Graduation NFTs that are non-transferable and issued only after verified module completion; (4) an Academy system with Progress Tracker, Badge Tracker, and Verifier contracts for on-chain learning credentials; and (5) a Reputation contract that tracks user scores, tiers, and streaks, with cross-contract integration to automatically update NFT metadata on level-up.

KindFi integrates with Trustless Work for escrow infrastructure and uses a SubQuery indexer to stream on-chain events into a Supabase database for real-time UI. The live platform at kindfi.org already hosts active campaigns (clean water, healthcare, education) with real funding goals and milestone tracking. The project is supported by the Stellar Development Foundation and is an active participant in the Stellar Wave Program with 102 forks and an active open-source contributor community on Telegram.

projects.name: BeEnergy
projects.description:
BeEnergy is a social-impact infrastructure project in the Stellar Wave ecosystem focused on making renewable-energy certification more accessible to community cooperatives and small producers. The project combines a cooperative management dashboard with Soroban smart contracts so local energy groups can register members, track meter readings, validate generation, and tokenize renewable output as on-chain proto-certificates where 1 token represents 1 kWh. Its public mission is not generic climate branding: the repository explicitly targets cooperatives, members, meters, generation statistics, and certificate sales to external buyers such as companies, ESG funds, and climate programs. That creates a practical path for small renewable-energy communities to document production and participate in transparent certification workflows.

The beneficiary population includes cooperative members and prosumers whose electricity generation is often hard to certify in a verifiable, portable way. BeEnergy's published `energy_distribution` contract shows how the project uses Stellar to create fair allocation rules: once generation is recorded, certificates are distributed proportionally to cooperative members according to their participation percentages. Later, buyers can retire certificates, with Stellar preserving a cryptographic trail of mint and burn activity. The commercial payment itself is handled off-chain, but the proof of generation and retirement is anchored on-chain, which is the project's mechanism for transparent value distribution and impact accountability.

BeEnergy is verifiably part of the Stellar Wave Program through BuenDia-Builders, whose approved Drips Wave listing includes the `be-energy` repository. The public documentation also publishes a testnet admin account, three deployed Soroban contracts, and recent mint and burn transactions. Its testing docs report a full February 2026 pilot simulation covering 3 prosumers, 4,704 readings, 2,102.1 kWh of certified solar generation, and about 841 kg of avoided CO2. Those are published testnet demo metrics rather than audited production totals, but they still demonstrate a measurable model for positive social change built on Stellar.

projects.name: Nevo
projects.description:
Nevo is a social-impact project in the Stellar Wave ecosystem focused on transparent donation pools powered by Soroban smart contracts. The public repository describes Nevo as infrastructure for creating donation pools that can accept XLM, USDC, and custom Stellar assets, while giving donors a verifiable ledger trail for contributions and disbursements. Its core idea is to make charitable giving more transparent and more capital efficient than traditional platforms by combining low-fee Stellar transactions with programmable pool logic and optional DeFi yield generation on idle funds.

From a technical perspective, Nevo is split into a Rust Soroban contract workspace and a Next.js frontend. The smart-contract side implements crowdfunding and pool-management logic, while the frontend includes donation execution code that builds Soroban contract calls and references committed asset-contract addresses for supported donation assets. In the public frontend source, the donation flow prepares a `contribute` call and explicitly maps XLM and USDC to Soroban asset contracts, which provides verifiable on-chain identifiers even though pool-specific contract IDs are supplied dynamically at runtime. That structure suggests Nevo is being built as a reusable donations layer rather than a single static campaign contract.

Nevo is part of the Stellar Wave Program through Web3Novalabs, which is listed on the Drips Stellar Wave page with the Nevo repository under its Wave projects. Taken together, the Drips listing, the open-source Soroban contract code, and the publicly committed Stellar integration files make Nevo a credible Wave project at the intersection of public goods, on-chain transparency, and blockchain-native philanthropy.

projects.name: Trustless Work Smart Escrow
projects.description:
Trustless Work is a decentralized escrow infrastructure layer built specifically for the Stellar Soroban smart contract ecosystem. Its primary mission is to provide a permissionless, secure, and fully automated framework for conditional payments, effectively eliminating the need for centralized intermediaries in global trade and service delivery. Each escrow instance operates as an isolated, independent smart contract that maintains its own logic, participant roles, and USDC balances directly on the ledger. This architecture ensures that funds are only released when pre-defined milestones are met, providing a level of security that traditional payment processors cannot match.

The target audience for this infrastructure is broad, spanning from DeFi protocols requiring secure treasury management to freelance marketplaces and P2P rental services like StellarRent. Key technical features include advanced milestone-based release schedules, automated dispute resolution via multi-sig or third-party oracles, and native integration with Stellar’s high-speed stablecoin rails. By offering these plug-and-play escrow primitives, Trustless Work powers real-world utility apps such as Stellopay for automated payroll and SafeTrust for peer-to-peer asset trades. This project is a vital component of the Stellar Wave Program because it transitions the network from a simple payment rail to a programmable financial layer capable of handling complex, real-world business logic with zero-trust requirements. Furthermore, as an infrastructure project, it provides the developer tools and SDKs necessary for other builders to integrate secure escrow functionality into their own dApps without having to write complex smart contract logic from scratch.
